problem: World-model-augmented visual spatial reasoning (e.g., MindJourney) invokes imagination in a fixed, always-on, exhaustive way, ignoring whether extra views are needed. This is costly and can add misleading or redundant views that hurt accuracy.
motivation: Imagination is only useful for some queries: on SAT-Real, 54% of instances are already correct without the world model and only 14% are helped by it. More imagined views give non-monotonic gains, and always-on imagination costs about 100x tokens and 30x time for a 4.6% gain. A selective-imagination oracle reaches 75.3% versus 66.6% for always-on, so adaptive control has clear headroom.
key_idea: A policy MLLM first judges whether the current visual evidence is sufficient and decides skip or call_wm. If it calls, it proposes short low-level action plans that are sampled multiple times, rendered by a world model, and scored by a trajectory-level verifier before answering.
insight: Imagination is mainly useful for action-conditioned reasoning (+57.1% gain on those errors vs +28.5% for motion errors), and only 1-2 imagined views are needed (74.0 to 80.0 on SAT). In the ablation, gating alone cuts world-model calls to 0.51 but drops accuracy to 73.3%, while gating plus action scaling reaches 79.3% with 0.73 calls, so both 'when' and 'how' matter. Gating is still imperfect (recall 43.9%, precision 27.1% on error cases), and the QA model's spatial ability is the main bottleneck.
method: Policy gating: the MLLM outputs d in {skip, call_wm} from observation, question and choices; on call_wm it also outputs a 1-6 step plan over move-forward 0.25 m / turn-left 9° / turn-right 9°.
Policy-level test-time scaling: the policy is sampled M times (default 5) and the gating decision is made by majority vote for self-consistency.
World model execution: the Stable Virtual Camera (SVC) renders imagined views only for the policy-proposed action sequences, instead of exhaustive beam search (about 12.34 calls in MindJourney).
Trajectory-level verifier: the same MLLM scores each whole imagined trajectory on a 0-9 usefulness scale, and the top one is kept, unlike MindJourney's per-keyframe scoring.

Final QA: the VLM answers from the original views plus the selected imagined views, or from the original views alone if skipped. The policy, verifier and QA share one base MLLM with different prompts, and there is no fine-tuning.
Navigation integration: inside MapGPT's step-wise nav-graph pipeline, the policy picks views to imagine from, and the imagined views are added to the view set before predicting the next node.

setting.backbone: Frozen MLLMs (InternVL3-14B, GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, o1) for policy, verifier and QA; SVC as the world model
setting.observation: one or multiple egocentric RGB images (SAT, MMSI); navigation-graph views for R2R
setting.action_space: Imagination actions: move-forward 0.25 m, turn ±9° (discrete). Navigation: choose the next node in the nav graph (MapGPT).
setting.simulator: Matterport3D simulator (R2R, via MapGPT); SAT and MMSI are static image benchmarks

The R2R split is not stated explicitly and is assumed to be val-unseen from the 72-scene MapGPT setting. The text says o1 reaches 81.3% while Table 1 prints 85.3 (Table 7 lists o1+o1 at 81.3), so the table figure is used here. The 'Acc' metric on SAT is the Avg. column.
results: On SAT-Real, AVIC raises GPT-4.1 from 74.0 to 79.3, above MindJourney's 77.3, with 0.73 world-model calls versus 12.34 and far fewer tokens (7.6K vs 67.1K). It also raises InternVL3-14B from 59.3 to 74.6 (MindJourney 66.7) and o1 from 74.6 to 85.3 (MindJourney 77.3); with GPT-4o (68.0) it falls slightly below MindJourney's 69.3. It also helps on MMSI-Bench (GPT-4.1 30.9 to 33.8) and gives a small gain on R2R over MapGPT with GPT-4o (SR 36.0 to 37.5, SPL 30.8 to 31.9).
limitations: The gating policy is imprecise: recall 43.9% and precision 27.1% on error cases needing imagination, and it over-triggers on egocentric-movement tasks.
Gains depend on the QA model and the SVC world model; GPT-4o with AVIC is slightly below MindJourney on SAT, and the R2R and MMSI improvements are small.
Evaluation is on small benchmarks (SAT-Real), and R2R is a 72-scene subset with GPT-4o that is lower than MapGPT GPT-4 in SR and OSR.
